summary: Build digital OHS skills for inspections, incident reporting, IoT monitoring, and dashboards. Create a practical implementation roadmap with TrainingCred.
lede: Digital transformation of occupational health and safety management helps connect inspections, incident records, exposure readings, and corrective actions into a more reliable operating model. This course develops practical skills for mapping safety workflows, choosing fit-for-purpose digital tools, structuring data, validating controls, and reporting meaningful trends. You will practise designing mobile inspection workflows, classifying incident information, defining dashboard needs, assessing IoT sensor use cases, and planning staged implementation with adoption measures. Using ISO 45001, ISO 31000, Bowtie analysis, Job Safety Analysis, and the hierarchy of controls, the course shows how to turn connected safety information into prioritised risk controls and decision-ready reporting.
audienceIntro: Digital OHS is designed for professionals responsible for converting occupational health and safety requirements into reliable field processes, usable data, and accountable risk controls. It suits beginner to intermediate users of safety technology, including experienced OHS practitioners who need a structured digital transformation approach.
modules: OHS Analytics and Power BI Dashboards
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of workplace hazard identification, incident reporting, inspections, and basic risk assessment. Familiarity with ISO 45001 is useful but not essential. No coding or programming is required. You will work with supplied sample datasets and templates, and basic spreadsheet experience will help you interpret OHS indicators. Advanced analytics, IoT architecture, and cybersecurity topics receive conceptual or operational treatment rather than technical engineering instruction.
